text:
ashley: heads-up — after the runtime change that prefers the FlashAttention path we see an 8-12% throughput drop on small-seq workloads (seq <= 32). opening thread to collect profiling and tweak continuous-batcher heuristics.
omar: can you paste the perf summary? p50/p99 or tokens/sec?
ashley: p50 unaffected, p99 up ~30ms for tiny requests; tokens/sec down ~10% on our chat-heavy trace. quick profile: 
```
PROFILE small-seq workload (avg_seq=18):
- kernel-switch: flash_attn path selected 78%
- tokens/sec: 52k -> 47k (-9.6%)
- p99 latency: 210ms -> 240ms (+14%)
- batch_size distribution: median 6, tail >32 due to long polls
```
morgan: interesting — on my trace paged-KV promotions are happening mid-batch, causing extra memcpy and stalling the batcher. we see spike in CUDA memcpy latency at the same times.
rui: hypothesis: FlashAttention has lower arithmetic for long seqs but worse startup cost for very small sequences; kernel launch + workspace alloc kills tiny-batch efficiency. we should bias batch formation and token_budget targets to avoid too many tiny + flash combos.
omar: agree. propose two quick experiments: (1) per-batch kernel-choice based on avg_seq threshold (calc kernel_latency_est(avg_seq, batch_size)) and (2) queue policy: prioritize short-seq requests into a fast lane that prefers nv-attn kernel.
ashley: I'm leaning to option (2) first — simpler config change. config draft: 
```yaml
continuous_batcher:
  queue_policy: 
    - name: short_first
      max_seq: 32
      token_budget_target: 256
      max_wait_ms: 6
    - name: balanced
      token_budget_target: 1024
      max_wait_ms: 12
  kernel_selection: batch_level_decision: true
```
omar: can you run a microbench with token_budget_target=256 vs 512 for the short_first lane? I expect 256 to reduce latency variance and keep Flash from being selected when inefficient.
morgan: note on paged KV: when page-size is 64k and we promote cold keys into the hot cache during batch assembly, we see page faults that add ~4-6ms per affected request. we should avoid mixing requests that trigger KV promotes with the short lane. maybe add a KV-hit hint to request metadata.
rui: also add a small heuristic: if batch avg_seq < 40 and batch_stddev < 12, favor non-flash kernel. we can model kernel latency with a tiny polynomial and use it in the scheduler. i ran a quick fit: 
```
latency_flash(avg_seq, b) = 0.45 + 0.012*avg_seq + 0.0012*b  # ms per token-ish estimate
latency_nv(avg_seq, b) = 0.5 + 0.009*avg_seq + 0.0015*b
```
then pick kernel with lower predicted tail.
perf-bot: regression-detect: eng/runtime/flash-path rolled out at 1754319000 -> flagged throughput drop on "chat_small_seq" test.
deploy-bot: canary: rolling config change to 10% of hosts for 30m window. patch id: rbw-canary-1754321.
ashley: plan: (A) canary short_first lane with token_budget_target=256, KV-hit isolation for short lane, and batch-level kernel decision off by default. (B) run perf-suite with historic chat trace and the reg test. (C) if green, ramp and enable batch-level kernel selection.
omar: i'll add a perf-suite job and an artifact with the per-batch kernel decisions so we can replay and analyze. also will log batch composition (avg_seq, stddev, kv_promotes).
morgan: if canary shows KV promote regressions, i can instrument paged-kv to prefer async prefetch for known active keys (cheap opt).
rui: note for long-term: we should expose a small cost-model endpoint in the runtime so console/optimize can recommend token_budget and queue_policy per customer workload.
ashley: thanks all — i'll open the canary PR with the yaml above and a short perf checklist. expecting initial results in ~30m. :thumbsup:
